articles.title: Design com autoria compõe os ambientes da Vectra | G1
articles.standfirst: Curadoria reúne peças de designers e arquitetos de destaque nacional e valoriza também artistas de Londrina.
articles.summary: Curadoria reúne peças de designers e arquitetos de destaque nacional e valoriza também artistas de Londrina.
articles.body:
A seleção vai ao encontro do que a empresa valoriza em seus projetos e ambientes corporativos: unir estética e sofisticação à funcionalidade. A arte entra como elemento que contribui para dar identidade própria aos espaços, com objetos caracterizados pela qualidade dos materiais, precisão no acabamento, ergonomia, conforto e atemporalidade.

No acervo da Vectra, destacam-se criações do arquiteto e designer Sergio Rodrigues, reconhecido internacionalmente; do arquiteto e designer londrinense Fabricio Roncca; da Terinn Arquitetura, de Londrina; e do premiado designer de mobiliário brasileiro Mauricio Bomfim.

Para a diretora executiva da Vectra, Roberta Costa Alves Nunes Mansano, existe uma relação entre a maneira como esses objetos são concebidos e os valores que a empresa busca levar para seus próprios projetos.

"Peças de design carregam história e tradição, exigem atenção ao detalhe, o desejo de fazer daquilo algo único. São características que a gente se espelha. Buscamos inspiração nessa forma de concepção de produto, feita com muito cuidado e estudo" , afirma.

As poltronas Cigarra, assinadas pela Terinn Arquitetura, compõem o mobiliário da sede da Vectra. — Foto: Divulgação.

A arquiteta Chris Brasil, responsável pelos projetos de interiores da sede da Vectra e pela maioria dos decorados da construtora, explica que a definição dos itens parte do perfil de morador imaginado para cada empreendimento. A partir daí, alguns móveis assumem o papel de elemento central, um sofá, uma poltrona, algo capaz de organizar visualmente o espaço. "Aí, iniciamos a pesquisa sobre quem são os profissionais responsáveis pelo desenho e o que faz sentido para aquele projeto" , conta Chris.

No decorado do Oscar, por exemplo, uma das escolhas foi uma poltrona assinada por Sergio Rodrigues, nome de referência no design brasileiro e contemporâneo de Oscar Niemeyer, arquiteto que inspirou o projeto da Vectra, que traz elementos do modernismo. O apartamento também recebeu quadros de Elvio Nóbrega, artista de Londrina, com importantes construções de Brasília bordadas à mão.

Poltrona assinada por Sérgio Rodrigues decora a sala do apartamento do Oscar. — Foto: Divulgação/Ana Pacheco.

Detalhe de um dos quadros de Elvio Nóbrega, bordado à mão. — Foto: Divulgação/Ana Pacheco.

Já no Lina, inspirado na arquiteta ítalo-brasileira Lina Bo Bardi, o projeto incorporou peças desenhadas especialmente para o ambiente, como uma mesa e um móvel complementar ao sofá, em diálogo com a trajetória de Lina, conhecida pela criação de mobiliário e pela relação entre arquitetura, design e produção cultural. "Queríamos trazer essa coisa mais autoral. O quadro foi feito especificamente para o decorado, também por uma artista de Londrina, a Tosca. É um desenho feito à mão da obra do Sesc Pompeia" , detalha Chris.

Quadro inspirado no Sesc Pompéia decora o Lina. — Foto: Divulgação/Ana Pacheco.

A curadoria de mobiliário também valoriza o trabalho de artistas locais. Um exemplo é uma poltrona de Fabricio Roncca, arquiteto e designer londrinense premiado, que integra o acervo há anos. A Terinn Arquitetura assina a cadeira Cigarra, encontrada na sede da construtora em duas versões, com diferentes alturas de encosto.

Poltrona Vergara, assinada por Fabricio Roncca, é uma das peças de design do acervo da Vectra. — Foto: Divulgação/Divulgação.

Na recepção, o design aparece de forma ainda mais evidente. O sofá Fragmento, de Mauricio Bomfim, ocupa posição de destaque, acompanhado pela poltrona Fábula, do mesmo designer, que também assina as quatro poltronas Boto presentes na área de atendimento, todas com linhas curvas e formas orgânicas.

A recepção da Vectra traz mobiliário assinado por Mauricio Bomfim. — Foto: Divulgação.

Para Chris Brasil, hoje, há uma compreensão maior de que móveis com autoria não estão restritos a grandes centros. O lançamento de linhas comerciais facilitou o acesso a esse tipo de peça. "O cliente que valoriza a arte e o design quer algo que tem um porquê, que possui uma história" , confirma.

Com o passar dos anos, alguns desses objetos podem ainda ganhar outro significado. É o caso de determinados móveis de Sergio Rodrigues, já tratados no mercado como peças de coleção. "É uma forma de investimento, é algo que você vai deixar para o seu filho, uma herança. Existem peças que têm valor de obra de arte" , diz Chris.

A curadoria ajuda a construir a identidade de cada ambiente e cria uma conexão entre o espaço contemporâneo e profissionais que deixam sua marca no design brasileiro. Ao colocar esses objetos no cotidiano, a Vectra reforça uma escolha presente em sua trajetória, a de tratar a arte como parte da experiência de seus projetos e dos espaços que cria.

articles.title: Ivete Sangalo e Bell Marques são anunciados na Virada Salvador | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo prefeito Bruno Reis (União), atrações se apresentarão no dia 31 de dezembro, dia da virada de ano. Ordem, datas e demais artistas ainda não foram divulgados.
articles.summary: Segundo prefeito Bruno Reis (União), atrações se apresentarão no dia 31 de dezembro, dia da virada de ano. Ordem, datas e demais artistas ainda não foram divulgados
articles.body:
Ivete Sangalo e Bell Marques são anunciados no Festival Virada Salvador — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Os cantores Ivete Sangalo e Bell Marques foram confirmados na programação do Festival Virada Salvador deste ano. A informação foi compartilhada pelo prefeito Bruno Reis (União) nas redes sociais, nesta segunda-feira (21).

Os dois são os primeiros a serem anunciados para a festa. Segundo o gestor municipal, os artistas se apresentarão em 31 de dezembro, dia da virada do ano.

"A imprensa perguntou e eu, que tenho boca de sacola, larguei o doce: esse ano, no dia 31/12, a gente vai ter Bell e Ivete no Virada Salvador!", escreveu o prefeito.

No entanto, ainda não foram detalhados os horários dos shows. A prefeitura também deve anunciar em breve as datas e as demais atrações da festa em comemoração ao Réveillon.

Tradição em Salvador, o evento passou a ser realizado na Arena O Canto da Cidade, na orla do bairro da Boca do Rio, desde a virada entre os anos de 2017 e 2018.

Na maioria das últimas edições, foi de responsabilidade de Ivete Sangalo comandar a contagem regressiva para o novo ano.

Além dela e de Bell Marques, já passaram pelos palcos do evento nomes como Léo Santana, Tony Salles, Daniela Mercury, Anitta e Iza.

articles.title: Festival Regional de Turismo movimenta Saquarema | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento gratuito reúne municípios, especialistas e empreendedores para debater políticas públicas e novas tendências do setor.
articles.summary: Evento gratuito reúne municípios, especialistas e empreendedores para debater políticas públicas e novas tendências do setor.
articles.body:
1°Festival Regional de Turismo da Costa do Sol divulga programação de três dias em Saquarem — Foto: Divulgação

Começa nesta segunda-feira (21) e vai até quarta-feira (23), o 1º Regional Festival de Turismo da Costa do Sol, que acontece no Centro de Eventos de Saquarema , na Região dos Lagos do Rio. O encontro é gratuito e aberto ao público, com programação diária das 13h às 17h.

A programação abordará políticas públicas, regionalização do turismo, segurança nas atividades de aventura, captação de recursos e tendências como turismo pet friendly, rural e sustentável.

Também estão previstas uma apresentação sobre a trajetória e os novos projetos turísticos de Saquarema, cidade anfitriã, e uma atividade extra do Geoparque Costões e Lagunas do Rio de Janeiro, na Casa da Pedra.

Um dos principais momentos do encontro será a realização de cinco câmaras setoriais, nas quais os participantes poderão colaborar diretamente na construção de propostas para o desenvolvimento turístico da região.

Nesta segunda-feira (21) o Painel Federal discute políticas nacionais, regionalização, programas e mecanismos de fomento ao turismo. Às 15h, o Painel Estadual aborda fomento turístico, integração e governança regional. O encerramento do primeiro dia acontece às 16h, com uma apresentação artística.

Na terça-feira (22) a programação conta com uma atividade extra do Geoparque Costões e Lagunas do Rio de Janeiro, realizada na Casa da Pedra. O projeto atua na valorização e na divulgação do patrimônio geológico, ambiental, histórico e cultural dos municípios que integram o território reconhecido como geoparque.

Não é necessário possuir CNPJ, integrar uma instituição formal ou apresentar um projeto previamente elaborado para participar. Cada interessado pode escolher a câmara com a qual mais se identifica e na qual acredita que podecontribuir de maneira mais direta.

No quarta-feira (23), a programação fala sobre Segurança no Turismo de Aventura. Às 14h40, será abordado o tema “Captação de Recursos: desmistificando convênios e instrumentos de fomento”.

Às 15h, o Painel Tendências Turísticas discute quatro segmentos que vêm ampliando sua presença no mercado: turismo pet friendly, turismo rural e turismo sustentável.

Às 16h, será apresentado o Projeto QualificaTur Costa do Sol, voltado à qualificação profissional nos setores de hotelaria e gastronomia. O encerramento do Festival acontece às 16h10, com uma apresentação artística.

A participação no Festival é gratuita, mas exige inscrição, que poderá ser realizada antecipadamente ou no próprio local. Para evitar filas e agilizar o credenciamento, a organização recomenda o preenchimento prévio do formulário disponível.

Os ônibus de turismo responsáveis pelo transporte de participantes do Festival terão isenção da taxa de entrada em Saquarema durante o período oficial do evento e das atividades relacionadas à programação.

Para receber o benefício, a empresa ou o responsável pelo veículo deverá solicitar previamente o credenciamento por meio deste site .

articles.title: 'Love & War': Sanjay Leela Bhansali to reshoot war portions with Ranbir Kapoor, Alia Bhatt and Vicky Kaushal
articles.summary: Three weeks after 'Love & War' had officially wrapped, Sanjay Leela Bhansali decided he wasn't quite finished with it. Reports suggest the filmmak.
articles.body: Three weeks after 'Love & War' had officially wrapped, Sanjay Leela Bhansali decided he wasn't quite finished with it. Reports suggest the filmmaker, known for his exacting standards, wasn't fully satisfied with how the war sequences turned out, so he's brought Ranbir Kapoor, Alia Bhatt, and Vicky Kaushal back to set. Bhansali is said to be personally supervising the reshoots to get the battle portions right.A week-long shoot at Welcome MaidaanAccording to Mid-day, Bhansali will spend about a week filming the battle portions at Welcome Maidaan in Goregaon. He is extremely particular about how the war portions come together because they are integral to the film’s scale and emotional arc. Once he saw the material in the edit, he felt certain battle portions could be enhanced further. They are not changing what has already been shot, but are simply perfecting the sequence.Bhansali had already put in extensive shooting time at Royal Palms in Goregaon during 'Love & War's' final schedule. He's now personally supervising these additional scenes while working on the edit in parallel. There were also reports of the filmmaker planning to shoot one more song for the film, but that idea has reportedly been shelved for now.Ranbir Kapoor's upcoming projectOn the professional front, Ranbir Kapoor's next release is Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana,' co-starring Sai Pallavi, Yash, and Sunny Deol. articles.title: Steven Spielberg surprised Ke Huy Quan with a $100,000 paycheck after ‘Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom’; actor reveals: 'Mom was holding an envelope with my name printed across it'
articles.summary: In his memoir 'Never Say Die', Ke Huy Quan recounts the touching moment when he received a $100,000 paycheck from Steven Spielberg after starring in 'Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom'. This unexpected gesture from the director and producer George Lucas highlights the generosity in Hollywood during the film's impressive box office success.
articles.body: Ke Huy Quan, who started his career in Hollywood at just 12 years old with Harrison Ford in ‘Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom,' recently opened up about starring in the film. In his recently released memoir, ‘Never Say Die,' the beloved actor opened up about a surprising incident from his time working on the film and how producer George Lucas and director Steven Spielberg gave him a surprise.Ke Huy Quan talks about Steven Spielberg’s surprise after ‘Indiana Jones'The actor recently published his memoir, ‘Never Say Die,' which encompasses his time in the industry, not getting any work, and getting a boost in his career with ‘Everything Everywhere All At Once.' In an excerpt from the book, as reported by Entertainment Weekly, Quan opened up about a pleasant surprise that the film's producer, George Lucas, and the award-winning director, Spielberg, left him with after the ‘Indiana Jones’ film was released.In an industry where most actors did not receive compensation from the film’s box office profits, he revealed that he received a cut after the adventure film made more than USD 300 million at the box office. He shared in the book, “One afternoon, I walked into the kitchen and found my parents standing together at the table. Mom was holding an envelope with my name printed across it. Dad had the papers that had been inside.” Quan had already been paid for his role in the film; however, the director and producer sent him an additional check.“They were both smiling, the kind of smile that comes from surprise and disbelief mixed together. They handed everything to me. It was a check from Lucasfilm. It was for almost $100,000, an amount that didn’t make any sense to me," he added. The actor also shared, “Back then, almost no actors got a piece of a movie’s profits. Even today, only the biggest stars do. That a kid like me, making his first film, would be included in something like that was unheard of. And Temple of Doom wasn’t some small movie no one was expected to see. It was the sequel to a massive hit, a movie everyone knew would make a lot of money. That made their gesture even more generous.”Calling it a life-changing moment for his family, Quan also commented on how much the extra money meant to his family.For the unversed, Ke Huy Quan played the young sidekick ‘Short Round,' a witty Chinese orphan in ‘Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom’ (1984), who accompanied Jones throughout all of his adventures. Quan scored the role after casting calls and auditions were held at his elementary school. Prior to this, he had never acted before.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'Angikaaram' OTT release date: When and where to stream Kotapadi J Rajesh and Sindhoori Vishwanath's sports drama
articles.summary: Tamil sports drama 'Angikaaram' is set to make its digital debut following its theatrical release earlier this year. The movie, which features Kotapad.
articles.body: Tamil sports drama 'Angikaaram' is set to make its digital debut following its theatrical release earlier this year. The movie, which features Kotapadi J Rajesh and Sindhoori Vishwanath was directed by Thenpathiyan. The film marks Kotapadi J Rajesh's debut as a feature filmmaker.When will 'Angikaaram' release on OTT?'Angikaaram' will begin streaming on Sun NXT on September 25. The streaming service shared the OTT update with a caption that gives a glimpse into the film's central conflict. "His only crime was daring to dream. Based on true events."What is 'Angikaaram' about?The movie centres on Aathiran played by Kotapadi J Rajesh. He is a talented runner who comes from a financially struggling family. His sporting abilities give him an opportunity to compete at the Commonwealth Games.However his path to the international sporting event is disrupted when his name is removed from the selection. Aathiran refuses to accept the decision quietly and takes the matter to court. His legal battle brings him into conflict with people who hold great influence within the sporting system. The story explores his attempt to challenge the circumstances that threaten his career.'Angikaaram' explores an athlete's struggleThe film uses Aathiran's journey to examine the difficulties faced by athletes without influential support. The conflict eventually takes the protagonist into the courtroom. His fight becomes more than an attempt to reclaim a place in a sporting event. Mansoor Ali Khan plays a minister connected to the conflict. Rama portrays Aathiran's mother, while Sindhoori Vishwanath is also part of the principal cast.What did ETimes say about 'Angikaaram'?ETimes gave 'Angikaaram' 2.5 stars out of 5. The review highlighted Kotapadi J Rajesh's performance and his physical preparation for the role."What keeps it watchable is Rajesh. For a producer turned actor, his debut is committed and physically convincing, with a real athlete's build and effort behind it. Ghibran's score works hard to pump in an urgency the writing mostly lacks. The subject, the way institutional politics smothers talent from the bottom rungs, deserves a film."The review also noted the contribution of composer Ghibran, particularly in creating intensity during the film's dramatic portions. articles.summary: 'Hanuman Ansh' continues its remarkable late-stage box office run, entering Day 46 with its India net collection now standing at Rs. 272.09 crore. Wha.
articles.body: 'Hanuman Ansh' continues its remarkable late-stage box office run, entering Day 46 with its India net collection now standing at Rs. 272.09 crore. What began as a slow, underwhelming opener has turned into one of the most unlikely long-haul successes of the year, powered by devotee support and sustained word-of-mouth, with the film's worldwide gross now inching towards the Rs. 350 crore mark. With its India net collection already at Rs. 272.09 crore, 'Hanuman Ansh' now has the Rs. 275 crore domestic mark firmly within reach, a milestone it could breach within the day given its current pace. On the global front, with the worldwide gross already past Rs. 347 crore, a push towards Rs. 350 crore looks imminent, keeping the film's extraordinary long-run success firmly intact as it continues to defy expectations set during its underwhelming opening weeks.'Hanuman Ansh's domestic box office runThe film’s theatrical journey has been defined by a significant turnaround. 'Hanuman Ansh' started with just Rs. 1.08 crore in its opening week, followed by Rs. 0.40 crore in Week 2. However, its fortunes changed dramatically from Week 3, when it collected Rs. 10.40 crore.The film then delivered Rs. 61 crore in Week 4, Rs. 90.25 crore in Week 5 and Rs. 80.25 crore in Week 6, taking its cumulative India net to Rs. 243.38 crore before the seventh-weekend earnings. It subsequently added Rs. 5 crore on Day 43, Rs. 9.75 crore on Day 44 and Rs. 13.75 crore on Day 45, taking the total to Rs. 271.88 crore.‘Hanuman Ansh’ overseas collection and worldwide totalThe film has also maintained a strong overseas contribution during its extended theatrical run. After Day 45, its overseas gross stood at Rs. 26 crore, while the India gross had reached Rs. 321.05 crore. This put the worldwide gross at Rs. 347.05 crore at the end of Day 45.'Hanuman Ansh' Day 46 collection live trackingAs per Sacnilk, 'Hanuman Ansh' is currently running across 5,870 shows on Day 46, having added a live collection of Rs. 1.74 crore so far in the day.This takes the film's overall India gross to Rs. 323.11 crore and its India net to Rs. 273.62 crore, with the final Day 46 figure expected once all shows for the day have concluded.Day wise collections for 'Hanuman Ansh'Week 1: Rs. 1.08 croreWeek 2: Rs. 0.40 croreWeek 3: Rs. 10.40 croreWeek 4: Rs. 61.00 croreWeek 5: Rs. 90.25 croreWeek 6: Rs. 80.25 croreDay 43: Rs. 5.00 croreDay 44: Rs. 9.75 croreDay 45: Rs. 13.75 croreDay 46 [LIVE]: Rs. 1.74 croreTOTAL: Rs. 273.62 croreMore about 'Hanuman Ansh'Directed and written by Vishal Chaturvedi, Hanuman Ansh is a spiritual drama inspired by the life, teachings and legacy of Neem Karoli Baba. The story follows a young boy who, after suffering a devastating loss, embarks on a transformative spiritual journey. The film explores themes of faith, compassion, humility and selfless service. Shobhinaw Satyaa leads the film, with Vihaan Shedge, Chandan K Anand, Purnima Tiwari, Anil Rastogi and Gulshan Pandey among the other members of the cast. The film has been certified U by the CBFC and has a reported runtime of around 2 hours and 30 minutes. articles.body: For the past couple of days, Ed Sheeran has faced many challenges after the Macklemore row, with all of his supporting acts dropping out of the tour. It seems Ed Sheeran and his cousin Jethro Sheeran have fallen out after the ‘Shape of You’ singer’s cousin called him a coward over the recent event. Read ahead to know more about what he had to say.Ed Sheeran’s cousin Jethro Sheeran calls him out after the Macklemore rowThe pop singer’s cousin, Jethro Sheeran, recently took to his Instagram account to share his thoughts on Ed, calling him a coward over everything that has happened recently. He posted about the singer and shared, “You can’t silence me! Ed Sheeran is a coward!! I’m embarrassed about this photo, but it’s 10 years old!" He shared a screenshot of a Facebook post with the same phrase written on it. He also shared an old photo of the two of them embracing, which he references in his comment.In another post shared on his page three days ago, Jethro stated he is “ashamed” of his cousin, adding, “Finally the world and all his fans see through him. He’s not a good person; I don’t like his music, so I can’t say he’s even a good artist. He’s honestly a selfish individual with malicious, cunning ways. ‘He kills you with kindness’ (His Words). I’m his first blood cousin, and he screwed me over and made fun of my mental health and mental health in general.”Calling him a “bad human," he mentioned, “He only cared about himself, and he puts out a fake narrative that’s calculated just to keep everyone happy so he can do big private gigs and keep brand deals, etc.”Ed Sheeran says that his family has abandoned himEd Sheeran recently broke down on stage while performing in Philadelphia over the weekend. Addressing the ongoing situation with Macklemore and his pro-Palestine comments, he read a statement about the saga. Videos of the artist were shared online, where he opened up about seeing the truth about many people.He added, in a video captured by a fan, the singer said, "In these situations you really find out who your friends are. It's been a weird week. It happened very quickly. At the same time, I had so many people telling me to cancel this tour, and so many people I've known for years and years and years, they're kind of backing away."He continued as the crowd of 50,000 attendees listened and cheered, adding, "In the back of my mind, I saw the ticket sales for this gig, and I didn't see cancellations; I saw people buying tickets for this gig. Everyone's telling me to cancel, and I'm feeling like all of my friends and family and people I know abandon me."Sheeran has expressed on multiple occasions that the decision to remove Macklemore from his ‘LOOP’ tour was not his. He shared that he attempted to mediate the situation with venues and organisers; however, the decision was never in his hands. Despite the explanation, the singer has faced significant backlash online from netizens, fans, and fellow celebrities in the industry.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: MrBeast responds to backlash after spending $10,000,000 in Ghana
articles.summary: MrBeast hits back at critics, saying he already supports North Carolina after launching a $10M village in Ghana.
articles.body:
YouTuber and philanthropist MrBeast has hit back at criticism after he spent nearly $10,000,000 on building a village in Ghana to prevent illegal child labor.

The new village includes homes, a school, water infrastructure and farms. But one X user questioned why MrBeast was funding a major project overseas and not giving more to his hometown of Greenville, North Carolina .

MrBeast was quick to share his charitable works in his hometown Greenville, North Carolina, where he said he has distributed millions from his charitable foundation, Beast Philanthropy.

Newsweek reached out to MrBeast via email for comment.

MrBeast, real name Jimmy Donaldson, is the most-subscribed individual creator on YouTube . Famed for extreme challenge videos , he often gives winners life-changing cash rewards totaling thousands and even millions of dollars.

Born in 1998, Donaldson first went viral in 2017 and has largely made his millions with investments and traditional media partnerships.

Now he is well known not just for his online content, but for his philanthropist work . Donaldson set up his own nonprofit, Beast Philanthropy , and has an impressive history of charitable works, from building homes for families in need to large cash giveaways.

One of MrBeast's latest videos documents the construction of a nearly $10 million "self-sustaining" village in Ghana aimed at reducing child labor in cocoa-growing communities.

According to MrBeast's video, the village includes a school with room for more than 300 students, 10 homes for teachers, a medical clinic, community marketplace, clean water infrastructure, solar power systems, agricultural facilities and free school meals for students for the next five years.

But as media coverage focused on this huge undertaking by the YouTuber, one response on X said: "I wonder why MrBeast doesn't do more for his hometown of Greenville, North Carolina, where the poverty rate is 25 percent (more than double the national average)?"

U.S. Census Bureau data shows 24.6 percent of people live in poverty in Greenville, nearly double the rate in North Carolina (12.5 percent) and more than double the U.S. rate (10.2 percent).

The YouTuber quickly responded. Sharing the work that he does in North Carolina, he said: "I literally do. I have a 501c non profit and have [distributed] 10s of MILLIONS of meals in America, many in my local community. If I listed all the philanthropic things we do locally I literally wouldn't be able to fit it in this tweet."

MrBeast's net worth is widely estimated at about $2.6 billion, though there is no official figure, and most of that wealth is thought to be tied to his ownership stake in Beast Industries rather than liquid cash.

MrBeast's Most Notable Philanthropic Efforts

As well as the huge Ghana project, the YouTuber continues to use his registered nonprofit to support causes around the world, some of his most notable efforts include:

Launched in late 2020 as part of Beast Philanthropy, Beast Pantry is focused in Greenville, North Carolina, where a food distribution model has reached communities around Eastern North Carolina, including places where traditional food pantries do not exist.

The system now counts more than 48 million meals delivered to people in need and more than 15 million people fed.

In 2019, MrBeast set up # TeamTrees with fellow YouTuber Mark Rober, a challenge to plant 20 million trees around the world by 2020. In partnership with the Arbor Day Foundation, for each dollar donated a tree was planted in "a forest of high need around the globe."

The campaign reached its $20 million financial goal in just 56 days, and today the project continues with more than 25 million trees planted.

In 2021, MrBeast and Rober launched a follow-up environmental campaign to raise funds and remove trash from oceans, rivers and beaches.

The goal was to remove 30 million pounds of waste and raised funds were given to Ocean Conservancy and The Ocean Cleanup.

The project was again successful and as of 2026, the pair report they have removed more than 34 million pounds of trash from waterways and oceans.

In 2023, MrBeast released the YouTube video titled "1,000 Blind People See For The First Time."

As part of the video, he paid for cataract surgeries for 1,000 people who could not afford treatment, sparking debate about healthcare affordability in the U.S.

Surgeries took place in the U.S. and countries including Jamaica, Honduras, Namibia, Mexico, Brazil, Indonesia, Vietnam, and Kenya.

Later in 2023, MrBeast repeated the idea, this time with hearing. In the video titled "1,000 Deaf People Hear for the First Time," he funded hearing aids and medical procedures for a thousand people with hearing impairments.

Alongside efforts in the U.S., MrBeast and his team also traveled internationally to assist people in Mexico, Guatemala, Brazil, South Africa, Malawi, and Indonesia.

For years, Beast Philanthropy has repeatedly responded to hurricanes, floods and other emergencies with support in the form of food, clothing, hygiene products and emergency supplies.

Most recently, Beast Philanthropy has paired with CARE to help fund the response to Nepal's floods where communities are still cut off by damaged roads and bridges.

articles.title: Princess Diana's brother Charles Spencer says King Charles 'gaslit' him over memoir claims
articles.summary: Charles Spencer says he was "gaslit" by King Charles III after Buckingham Palace questioned his memory of a shocking post-Diana conversation.
articles.body: Princess Diana's brother, Earl Charles Spencer, fired back at Buckingham Palace after the royal household questioned his recollection of a conversation with King Charles III, saying he was being "gaslit" by the monarch. Earlier this week, The Daily Mail published an excerpt of Spencer's upcoming memoir, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister," in which the king's former brother-in-law described having a heated conversation with Charles after Diana's death. In the excerpt, Spencer alleged that Charles said, "We’ll forget her soon enough!," regarding his ex-wife during their exchange. Buckingham Palace later responded to Spencer's claims, disputing the earl's account of the conversation and suggesting that grief may have affected his memory of events surrounding his sister's death. KING CHARLES DRAWS ‘LINE IN THE SAND’ WITH PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE AFTER COUPLE CAUGHT OFF GUARD: EXPERT During an interview with The Mail on Sunday, Spencer took issue with the palace's response. "It is not every day you wake up to find you've been gaslit by the king," he said. "It was astonishingly provocative and below the belt because it was essentially trying to say I'd lied without the King being able to deny what I'd said." "I also thought it was a rather poor imitation of the ‘recollections may vary’ quote, which was a much more elegant way of putting things, but in these circumstances entirely out of place," he added. The remark referenced the palace's famous "recollections may vary" statement issued after Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's explosive 2021 interview with Oprah Winfrey. In the excerpt, published Wednesday, Spencer described a phone call he said he had with Charles six days after Diana died in August 1997. "Prince Charles continued his stream of anger, without me interrupting. Then he stopped. I assumed the pause signaled an effort to bring himself under control, but then he unleashed down the phone what I have always taken to be his pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death," Spencer alleged. "‘Rest assured,’ he hissed, ‘we’ll forget her soon enough!’" PRINCESS DIANA'S HONEYMOON LETTER REVEALS A YOUNG BRIDE 'PLAYING WITH GROWN-UPS' IN THE ROYAL FAMILY According to the excerpt, the king and the 9th Earl of Spencer disagreed over the decision to have Prince William and Harry, then 15 and 12, walk behind their mother's casket during the funeral procession. KING CHARLES CONSIDERED QUEEN CAMILLA 'NON-NEGOTIABLE' AFTER PRINCESS DIANA, AUTHOR CLAIMS A Buckingham Palace spokesperson issued a rare statement responding to Spencer's claims. "While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and color memory in ways others do not recognize, even many years after such a loss," the statement said, according to People. Spencer stood by his account of the alleged conversation during an appearance on BBC One's "Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg." When Kuenssberg pointed out that Buckingham Palace had denied his version of events, Spencer pushed back, saying, "But they haven't actually, Laura. They've sort of smudged that one, haven't they?" Kuenssberg then read the palace's statement to Spencer, telling him that "the king is plainly furious." "Well, is he furious? Is he furious or is he embarrassed?" Spencer asked. "Because I can tell you here and now, those are exactly the words he said." Spencer said he remembered the conversation clearly because he had spoken so infrequently with Charles, who was then Prince of Wales. "I've only ever had two calls on the line with Prince Charles at any stage of my life," Spencer said. "I was hyper alert to what he was saying and those are precisely the words that he said." Spencer said he repeated the alleged comment to close friends and family members immediately afterward "because it was so monstrous." "Which, Charles, are the public meant to believe?" Kuenssberg asked. "Are they to believe you or are they to believe the king, the head of state of this country who's giving the impression very forcefully that this didn't happen? Who are we to believe?" "Well, I'm telling the truth," Spencer replied. "So, the king is giving an impression to the country that's not true. Misleading people, even lying?" Kuenssberg asked. "I can hardly be responsible for what Buckingham Palace says," Spencer replied. "All I can tell you is what was said and what I heard and what shocked me. What else would have made me hang up on the king that day? It was something as outrageous as that slur against Diana." When asked whether William and Harry would be upset by his account of the alleged phone call with their father, Spencer suggested his nephews were already familiar with his version of events. "Well, I don't like to talk about what I've been speaking about to William and Harry, but this will not be a surprise to them," he said. "I will tell you that these words will not be a surprise to them." A Buckingham Palace spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "We won’t be offering any comment." Diana died at age 36 after suffering injuries sustained in a car accident in the Pont de l'Alma tunnel in Paris, France. Her partner, Dodi Fayed, and the driver, Henri Paul, also died in the crash. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE At the time of her death, she and Charles had been divorced for about one year. The two married in July 1981, announced their separation in December 1992 and finalized their divorce in August 1996. Harry wrote about the decision to have him and his brother walk behind their mother's coffin in his 2023 memoir, "Spare," saying that "several adults were aghast" and that "mummy’s brother, Uncle Charles, raised hell," and that he told the royal family, "You can’t make these boys walk behind their mother’s coffin! It’s barbaric." Spencer previously spoke about his opposition to William and Harry walking behind their mother's coffin. He told BBC Radio 4's "Today" in 2017 that he found the decision "bizarre and cruel." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? It was the worst part of the day by a considerable margin, walking behind, well, my sister’s body, with two boys who were obviously massively grieving their mother. "But the feeling, the sort of crashing tidal wave of grief coming at you as you went down this sort of tunnel of deep emotion, it was really harrowing actually, and I still have nightmares about it now." articles.title: In 1942, Hedy Lamarr co-patented a torpedo communication system; 55 years later, her wireless innovation gained widespread recognition
articles.summary: Many people remember Hedy Lamarr as a famous Hollywood actress, but her contributions went far beyond movies and helped shape a broader legacy. During.
articles.body: Many people remember Hedy Lamarr as a famous Hollywood actress, but her contributions went far beyond movies and helped shape a broader legacy. During World War II, Lamarr worked with composer George Antheil on an unusual communication system designed to make radio-guided torpedoes harder for enemies to disrupt. Their invention received a U.S. patent in 1942, although its importance was recognised much later.More than five decades after the patent was granted, Lamarr and Antheil received recognition for their contribution to wireless communication. In 1997, the Electronic Frontier Foundation honoured the pair with its Pioneer Award, bringing renewed attention to an achievement that had largely remained outside Lamarr's Hollywood image.How did Hedy Lamarr's idea come about?Lamarr began developing the idea around 1940, when the threat of radio-controlled weapons was becoming an important military concern. She and Antheil explored a way to prevent an enemy from easily interfering with the signals guiding a torpedo.The basic principle was to keep changing the radio frequency instead of allowing a signal to remain on one channel. The transmitter and receiver would switch frequencies together, allowing the intended communication to continue while making interference more difficult. The Smithsonian's Lemelson Centre notes that Lamarr contributed the central idea, while Antheil helped with its practical implementation.Hedy Lamarr's 1942 patentLamarr and Antheil submitted their application for a "Secret Communication System" in June 1941. The U.S. patent, numbered 2,292,387, was granted in August 1942.The mechanism used synchronised changes between frequencies. The design also drew inspiration from player-piano technology, reflecting Antheil's experience with mechanical music systems. The patent was issued under Antheil's name and Lamarr's legal name at the time, Hedwig Kiesler Markey.Although the concept was presented to the U.S. Navy, it was not adopted during the period when the patent was active. The Smithsonian notes that several explanations have been discussed for the decision, including the practical difficulty of fitting the mechanism into a torpedo. The patent later expired in 1959.Why did the invention become important years later?Lamarr and Antheil's work eventually became part of the broader history of frequency-hopping and spread-spectrum communication. These ideas are connected to later developments in wireless communication, including technologies associated with Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and GPS.The National Inventors Hall of Fame describes Lamarr's frequency-hopping system as an important development in wireless communications. However, it is more accurate to say that her patented work contributed to the development of communication technology rather than claim that she directly invented modern Wi-Fi or Bluetooth.Hedy Lamarr received recognition 55 years after her patentThe gap between Lamarr's invention and the recognition it eventually received is one of the most striking parts of her story. In 1997, she and Antheil were honoured through the Electronic Frontier Foundation's Pioneer Awards for their contribution to wireless communication. Lamarr also became the first woman to receive the Invention Convention's BULBIE Gnass Spirit of Achievement Award, according to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences.Lamarr died in 2000, but interest in her work continued to grow. In 2014, she was posthumously inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame for the frequency-hopping communication system.From Hollywood star to inventorLamarr's legacy now exists across two very different worlds. She became famous for her screen career during Hollywood's Golden Age, while her collaboration with Antheil revealed another side of her interests and abilities.Her 1942 patent did not immediately transform military communication, but the idea behind it became part of a much larger technological story. Later recognition helped bring attention to Lamarr not only as a star but also as an inventor.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: While Katrina Kaif has built a successful career in Bollywood and established herself as an actor and entrepreneur, her mother Suzanne Turquotte has c.
articles.body: While Katrina Kaif has built a successful career in Bollywood and established herself as an actor and entrepreneur, her mother Suzanne Turquotte has chosen a very different path. Away from the spotlight and comforts associated with fame, Suzanne has spent years working for underprivileged children and communities in rural Tamil Nadu.Suzanne, who was based in London, moved to Tamil Nadu in 2008 and founded the NGO Relief Projects India. Her initial focus was on providing free evening tuition to children studying in government schools in rural communities. Over the years, the initiative expanded into a broader community development organisation with programmes focused on education, healthcare and child protection.In 2015, Suzanne also established Mountain View School. What began as a small nursery catering to fewer than 30 children, largely from economically disadvantaged villages, eventually developed into a nursery and primary school with more than 300 students.Katrina has often spoken about her mother’s dedication to charity and the impact it had on her upbringing. Speaking to ABP around a decade ago, she said, “My mom stays in Madurai where she has started a school for children. She is a teacher. She teaches there. And she is happy. It is because of her charities and blessings that I have reached these heights.”The actress also revealed that her mother’s lifestyle is far removed from the luxuries she herself enjoys today.“It is not easy to live there. They don’t have access to electricity. It is available for 12 hours. Sometimes, when I want to FaceTime my mother, I cannot, because there is no electricity or sometimes even internet. So we have a normal call,” Katrina added.For Katrina, her mother’s work was not something she discovered later in life. Charity and helping those in need had been part of her childhood and shaped the way she and her siblings grew up.Speaking to Colors Cineplex around seven years ago, Katrina recalled, “The countries that I grew up in when I was very young… they were always countries which had a lot of people who lived below the poverty line like we do here. It is something I have always been exposed to because my mom has done charity work. We didn’t grow up in a life of privilege or luxury. We had a very frugal and basic childhood. That’s the life I come from. I came from starting out, working in the industry and having absolutely no money. Needing to work to be successful and if I wouldn’t have been successful then I would have had to look for another job where I could have security.”Katrina also spoke about the school her mother built and continues to run.“She has this school in Madurai. This is a school she built from scratch. I think we have about 250 kids there. She teaches at the school. She has made curriculum, she trains the teachers there,” she said.The actress has also acknowledged how demanding her mother’s life in rural Tamil Nadu can be, particularly given the lack of basic conveniences.“A person who lives in a village where there are hours in a day when there is no electricity there. It’s incredibly hot and because you don’t have electricity, so the ACs are not there. She lives in this condition and she has always done because she enjoys helping people. It’s a tough life. It takes a different kind of person. I don’t know if I could do that. My mom has been there for more than 15 years I think,” Katrina said.Despite her demanding professional schedule, Katrina continues to support her mother’s work. She contributes a portion of her film earnings towards the school and has also used money earned through reality television shows to support the initiative.A source told Mid-Day, “Katrina loves the work her mother is doing and posts about it on social media sometimes. However, she doesn’t like to bring her contributions to attention. Since she is busy with her film commitments and hence cannot always visit the place, she donates money.”Suzanne was married to Mohammed Kaif, but the couple separated when Katrina and her siblings were young. She subsequently raised all eight children as a single mother while continuing her charitable work.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body: Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber’s son Presley Gerber had opened up about his battle with addiction and the fear he felt before undergoing an ibogaine treatment months before his death at the age of 27.Presley died on Sunday, September 20, at a rehabilitation facility in California, according to records from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. His cause of death has not been disclosed, with a postmortem examination pending. His family has asked for privacy during what it described as an “extremely difficult and painful time.”Presley Gerber spoke openly about his addiction treatmentIn March this year, Presley shared a deeply personal post documenting his experience at a treatment facility in Cancun, Mexico, where he underwent what he described as a “Pre-Ibogaine Flood Dose”.Ibogaine is a psychoactive compound derived from the iboga plant and has been investigated for its potential role in treating substance-use disorders. The treatment remains controversial and is not approved for medical use in the United States.Reflecting on the experience, Presley admitted that he had been frightened before undergoing the treatment.“I was absolutely terrified,” he wrote, adding that “letting go of control didn’t come easy” but that he trusted there was “something bigger than me guiding it.”Presley said he knew why he was at the clinic and described confronting things he had previously been “running from”.“I faced what I had been running from, and somewhere in all of it, I started finding my way back to myself,” he wrote, while hoping that it would be the last time he would need such treatment.Cindy Crawford called her son a ‘warrior’Presley’s post prompted emotional messages from his family.His mother, supermodel Cindy Crawford, praised him for his courage, writing, “You are a warrior! Walked thru the fire to find yourself! So proud!”His younger sister Kaia Gerber also commented on the post, writing, “That’s my brother I am so damn proud.”His father, Rande Gerber, similarly expressed his pride in his son.“I’m so proud of you and your courage. Facing what’s hard takes real strength and watching you find your way back to yourself is everything. I love you so much,” he wrote.Presley had described the treatment team at the Cancun facility as “incredible, caring, kind and on-their-s***”, and said he had also formed friendships during his time there.Presley had been candid about his mental health and substance-use strugglesThe model had increasingly spoken publicly about his mental health and addiction struggles in the years before his death.His sister Kaia recently discussed the impact of his decade-long struggle with drug addiction on their family in an interview with Vogue. She described Presley’s willingness to be open about his experiences as “refreshing” and said his honesty had changed the way the family approached difficult subjects.Presley had also previously spoken about depression, panic attacks and medication use. In December 2025, he discussed his treatment in a candid social media video, including medication prescribed for panic attacks and other mental-health difficulties.He had also launched a “Mental Health Mondays” series, using his own experiences to encourage conversations around mental health and addiction.In a 2023 podcast appearance, Presley spoke about wanting to use the mistakes he had made in his own life to help other people struggling with similar issues.What is ibogaine?Ibogaine is a naturally occurring psychoactive compound derived from the iboga plant, which is native to parts of Central Africa. It has attracted interest from researchers studying treatments for substance-use disorders, although it remains an experimental and controversial approach.A 2024 Stanford study involving veterans reported improvements in symptoms of depression, anxiety and functioning following ibogaine treatment, while researchers have continued to study its potential applications and risks.Ibogaine is not approved for medical use in the United States, where it is classified as a Schedule I controlled substance. It is nevertheless offered at specialised clinics in some countries, including Mexico.Importantly, there is currently no publicly disclosed evidence establishing a connection between Presley’s ibogaine treatment in March and his death in September. Authorities have not released his cause of death.Presley Gerber’s modelling careerPresley followed his mother into the fashion industry, beginning his modelling career as a teenager. He was signed by IMG Models and made his runway debut in 2016.He subsequently worked with major fashion brands including Calvin Klein and Dolce & Gabbana and appeared alongside Cindy Crawford in a 2018 Pepsi Super Bowl commercial.He also faced legal trouble in 2019 after being arrested for driving under the influence.Despite his professional success, Presley increasingly used his public platform to discuss his personal struggles, particularly mental health and addiction.Family asks for privacyFollowing news of his death, a representative for the Crawford-Gerber family confirmed the tragedy and asked the public to respect their privacy.“The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time,” the representative said.Presley’s death has also prompted tributes from friends and fellow celebrities, including Paris Hilton and Brooklyn Beckham, who shared emotional messages remembering the model.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Monty Python star Eric Idle, 83, says ‘I’d like to be buried here’ in Provence after surviving pancreatic cancer; recalls ‘rebirth’ talk with Beatles star George Harrison on his deathbed in 2001
articles.summary: Monty Python star Eric Idle has opened up about mortality, his battle with pancreatic cancer, his enduring connection with the French countryside and .
articles.body: Monty Python star Eric Idle has opened up about mortality, his battle with pancreatic cancer, his enduring connection with the French countryside and his life away from the spotlight. At 83, the comedian and writer says he has found a sense of peace in Provence, where he spends around half the year.“I’d like to be buried here,” Idle told Radio Times in a recent interview while looking across the picturesque corner of Provence he calls home. “But only after I’m dead.”Idle, best known as one of the members of the legendary comedy group Monty Python, has long been associated with irreverent humour and his mischievous on-screen persona. However, his reflections on death have become more personal after surviving pancreatic cancer, a disease he says could have killed him.Eric Idle on surviving pancreatic cancerIdle recalled the moment his doctor diagnosed him with pancreatic cancer. Rather than reacting with fear, he said he laughed because of an ironic coincidence.A year or two before his diagnosis, Idle had reportedly asked the same doctor which disease would be the quickest and most certain way to kill off a character in a musical he was writing. The answer was pancreatic cancer.The comedian has also developed an unusual connection with death through one of his most famous creations, “Always Look on the Bright Side of Life”, the Monty Python song that has become a popular choice at funerals.“I think having the number-one funeral song is pretty damn good. I love that, and I reckon it’s really healthy,” he said.Eric Idle recalls conversation with George Harrison about deathIdle also reflected on a conversation he had with Beatles legend George Harrison about death and what might come after it. The two discussed the idea of an afterlife while Harrison was on his deathbed in 2001.According to Idle, Harrison believed he would escape rebirth, while Idle told him, “I’d give anything to be reborn.”Asked what he would want to return as, Idle joked that he might choose to be an England Test cricketer - particularly from an era when players could still enjoy drinks in the evenings.Despite being responsible for some of Monty Python’s most enduring work, Idle remains modest about the group's legacy. He questioned whether Python’s comedy would remain funny forever, while acknowledging that its influence has continued across generations.Eric Idle's life in ProvenceIdle's affection for Provence is at the heart of his new book, Idle in Provence: A Brief History of Thyme. The memoir looks back at the property he bought in 1971, when it was little more than a ruined farm building without water, electricity, roads or even floors.Over the years, Idle transformed the property from what he jokingly calls a “shack to shackeau”.The book goes beyond renovation stories, offering a candid look at different chapters of his personal life. It touches upon his experiences following his divorce and the difficult period when his daughter was sectioned while he was preparing to perform at London's O2 during the 2014 Monty Python reunion.Idle says the original motivation behind buying the property was to escape the pressures and expectations surrounding his life in Britain, Monty Python and fame.“To escape! To escape the long shadow of boarding school, and how people are in England, and Python, and fame, which is a silly illusion that doesn’t help you much,” he explained.Hollywood stars found anonymity at Eric Idle's French homeThe secluded nature of Idle's home also attracted several of his famous friends over the years. According to the comedian, stars including Harrison Ford, Paul Simon, David Bowie, Carrie Fisher and Robin Williams enjoyed visiting the property, along with members of the Beatles, Rolling Stones, Pink Floyd and The Who.The appeal, he suggested, was the anonymity they could enjoy in the small French community of Cotignac, where their celebrity status mattered little.“No man is a legend to his trousers,” Idle quipped, deliberately altering a famous saying about a person not being a hero to their valet.Eric Idle claims John Cleese and Michael Palin will not returnWhile his French home hosted several Monty Python members over the years, Idle made a pointed remark about two of his former collaborators.Asked about John Cleese and Michael Palin, Idle said there was “absolutely zero” chance of either returning to his property.“They hate my guts. Don’t ask me why. I only ever made them money,” he said.Idle also spoke candidly about his finances and the realities of continuing to work at 83. Despite his decades-long career, he said he still works to cover his healthcare costs in the United States, where he lives when he is not in Provence.He also criticised the way streaming platforms handle royalties, arguing that people often assume performers from successful shows are financially secure decades later.Why Eric Idle wants to stay away from fameFor Idle, one of the biggest attractions of his life in Provence is the opportunity to exist without constantly being recognised as a celebrity.He described enjoying ordinary routines such as visiting the local bakery and supermarket and becoming part of the community.“I really don’t want to spend all day being mistaken for a comedian,” he said.Idle's new book offers readers an intimate look at the place that has provided him with that escape for decades. Yet he remains unconcerned that revealing details about his French retreat could attract unwanted visitors.Asked whether writing about his home could make it easier for people to find, Idle responded with another characteristically dark joke: “Oh, it’s hard to find. articles.title: Manoj Bajpayee moves Delhi High Court to protect personality rights from AI misuse - Report
articles.summary: Manoj Bajpayee has approached the Delhi High Court seeking protection of his personality rights, claiming his image, voice and identity are being misu.
articles.body: Manoj Bajpayee has approached the Delhi High Court seeking protection of his personality rights, claiming his image, voice and identity are being misused, including through artificial intelligence (AI) tools.Manoj Bajpayee moves court over misuse of identityThe 57-year-old actor filed the plea on Monday. He alleges that his likeness is being used to promote products and that AI is being used to copy his voice and parts of his personality. According to Live Law, the matter came up briefly before Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav. Senior Advocate Swathi Sukumar appeared for the actor.Allegations against the defendantsOne issue concerned H2PG Designs Private Limited. Manoj Bajpayee has claimed that the company used his photographs to suggest he was wearing suits made by it. Another defendant is accused of using AI to create the actor's voice. He has also raised concerns about AI chatbots borrowing elements of his personality.Why Delhi and not Mumbai?The court also raised the question of jurisdiction. Justice Kaurav asked why Manoj Bajpayee had come to Delhi when he is mainly based in Mumbai. Sukumar replied that some defendants are based in Delhi, which gives the court power to hear the case.The court suggested the suit could be heard and decreed, especially where defendants do not seem to contest such matters. Justice Kaurav observed that there was "no point of burdening ourselves" with such cases if the Registrar could routinely handle them instead of holding detailed hearings.Court asks for details of earlier ordersSukumar was asked to prepare a compilation of interim and final orders passed in earlier personality rights cases. She must also place on record how other High Courts have dealt with similar matters.Many celebrities already have similar protectionBajpayee's plea follows plenty of precedent. The Delhi High Court has earlier protected public figures such as Tabu, cricketers Abhishek Sharma and Yuvraj Singh, politician Shashi Tharoor and Deputy CM Pawan Kalyan.Orders have also come in favour of Allu Arjun, Mohanlal, Kajol, R Madhavan, Jr NTR, Sunil Gavaskar, Jubin Nautiyal, Aman Gupta and spiritual preacher Aniruddhacharya.Similar relief has been given elsewhere to Sri Sri Ravi Shankar, Nagarjuna, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, Abhishek Bachchan and Karan Johar. Salman Khan has also approached the court in a similar matter.Growing concern over AI misuseThe case reflects rising worry among public figures about unauthorised endorsements and AI-made content that copies their look and voice.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Paramount settles lawsuit blocking $110 billion Warner Bros. merger
articles.summary: Paramount has settled the antitrust lawsuit filed by 12 state AGs, which claimed its merger with Warner Bros. Discovery would harm the entertainment industry.
articles.body: Paramount has reached a settlement with California and the 11 other states that sued to block its planned $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. The settlement removes a major roadblock standing in the way of the massive media merger. According to the proposed consent decree filed with the court, it includes requirements like minimum numbers of theatrical film releases over the next five years, starting with 30 in year one and two, and 32 in the following years, and a commitment to spend at least $300 million more on production in the US compared to what the companies spent in 2025. At least four of the films produced must be independent films, and at least 20 percent must be “tentpole” blockbuster movies with $50 million-plus budgets, and releases on a minimum of 3,000 US screens within the first month. If Paramount doesn’t meet these film release requirements, it must divest Miramax Studios and pay $30 million per missed film. It also requires the merged company to keep offering a free streaming service, like Pluto TV, and includes a commitment not to sell Paramount Studios or Warner Bros. lots in California for at least five years. The settlement has rules for the negotiations over cable channels owned by the combined company as well, in addition to requirements for a news editorial independence board “made up of five established journalists” with at least ten years of experience to ensure editorial independence at CBS and CNN. At a press conference announcing the agreement, California AG Rob Bonta called the arrangement “the opposite” of the 2018 Disney-Fox deal, where Fox’s film output dropped afterward. “Let me be clear: This settlement is not a vote of support for this merger,” Bonta adds in a press release. “But we believe this settlement, which resolves our antitrust concerns in every market alleged in our case, protects competition and consumer choice, and puts workers’ needs, concerns, and futures first, is the best course of action.” > Paramount Chairman & CEO David Ellison: > We are grateful to Attorney General Bonta and his fellow AGs, as well as the WGA, for engaging in good faith to find a path forward to a resolution that serves all parties, and to Governor Newsom for his support throughout this process. Our shared aim was an outcome that best serves consumers, workers and — most importantly — the creative community so vital to the art of visual storytelling. We’re confident this agreement does exactly that, memorializing a series of commitments that include 30+ films annually and expanded U.S. film production to help revitalize our industry here at home. > Our goal has always been to build a stronger Hollywood — one with more stories told, greater choice for consumers and stronger competition. That vision was validated by unanimous approval from competition authorities in nearly 70 jurisdictions worldwide, who agreed this deal is pro-competitive, pro-consumer and pro-worker. Having now addressed the State AGs’ and WGA’s concerns, we have complete clearance for this merger and look forward to putting these commitments into action. Bringing Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery together will build that stronger Hollywood, creating expanded opportunity for our people and even more great entertainment for audiences around the world. The settlement comes just days before Paramount’s “ticking fee” was set to go into effect, which would require the entertainment giant to pay WBD shareholders 25 cents per share for each quarter the deal is delayed past September 30th. The fee would’ve cost Paramount about $7 million per day. [Media: Though the Trump administration signed off on the $110 billion merger, California, along with Arizona, Colorado, New York, Washington, and others, sued Paramount and WBD in July over antitrust concerns. They claimed the megamerger would create a “media behemoth” that would “inflict substantial harm” on the entertainment industry. A judge granted the states’ request to pause the merger shortly after. articles.title: Presley Gerber, son of Cindy Crawford, died from apparent overdose
articles.summary: Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber's son, Presley Gerber, died on Sept. 20 at age 27 from an apparent overdose, per the Santa Monica Police Department.
articles.body:
Presley Gerber 's death is being investigated as a suspected overdose , according to the Santa Monica Police Department.

The son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber died Sunday, Sept. 20, at the age of 27 at a rehab facility in the Los Angeles area. The SMPD announced in a press release issued Monday, Sept. 21, that it appeared to be the result of an overdose and there is no indication of foul play.

Additionally, the Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner completed an autopsy of Gerber's body Sept. 21, and the case has been deferred pending additional investigation, according to records viewed by USA TODAY.

A representative for Crawford and Rande Gerber previously confirmed their only son's death in a statement to USA TODAY: "The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time."

Cindy Crawford's son dies at 27. Look back at the famous family

Supermodel Cindy Crawford shares two children, Kaia and Presley , with husband Rande Gerber. Revisit the famous family in photos amid news of son Presley Gerber's death at age 27.

Presley Gerber spoke out about addiction, mental health

In recent years, the model had been open about his struggles with addiction and mental health. He even started a series on his social media talking about parts of his treatment and journey to recovery.

Gerber was the eldest child of Crawford and Rande Gerber, who have been married since 1998. They are also parents to model and actress Kaia Gerber , 25.

Crawford rose to fame as a supermodel in the 1980s and later launched a career in television and business. Rande Gerber is a hospitality entrepreneur known for his nightlife companies Midnight Oil and Gerber Group, as well as Gerber Spirits and the popular tequila brand Casamigos , which he cofounded with George Clooney.

Presley Gerber followed in his mother's footsteps and pursued modeling, landing major campaigns for brands like Calvin Klein and Dolce & Gabbana. In 2018, he and Crawford starred in a Pepsi commercial that aired during the Super Bowl.

The family has been outspoken about their support for Gerber's recovery. In an August Vogue interview, Kaia Gerber opened up about her brother's addiction and praised him for using his public platform to bring awareness to the matter.

"When something like that happens in a family, it kind of levels everyone," she said. "I think that's also why I started to self-​identify as the easy one and never wanted to ask for help. Because it felt like too much to have two children who were needing."

Gerber first discussed his depression, addiction and recovery during a 2023 appearance on the "Studio 22" podcast and later launched a "Mental Health Mondays" series on his social media, where he openly discussed his experiences.

Presley Gerber dies at 27. Revisit his modeling career

In March, he shared an Instagram post about undergoing an ibogaine treatment for addiction in Mexico. "Quiet moment before everything changed," he wrote in the caption, alongside a video of him before receiving the medication.

A Schedule I controlled psychoactive substance used to treat mental health problems and substance use disorders, ibogaine is not classified as a legal treatment in the United States and is banned in some countries due to its high risk for misuse. Among its several serious side effects are seizures, heart effects and dangerous behavior, according to WebMD .

"I was absolutely terrified, and I knew I would be again if I ever had to face something like this (helps to not go into the situations you do that get ya there but that's life sometimes.)," Gerber wrote in the Instagram post. "My mantras were love yourself and [it's] gotta be the last time for this reason. letting go of control didn't come easy, but I trusted there was something bigger than me guiding it. I knew why i was there."

He concluded: "I faced what I had been running from, and somewhere in all of it, i started finding my way back to myself 🤍…. We shall see…. Praying it's the last time I have to come back. Next time I'd like to choose 😜 🙏🏻"

He made his final public appearance months later at the We Are Enough x Aviator Nation launch event in Malibu, California, on June 11, where he participated in a panel about his experiences with mental health challenges.

If you or someone you know is struggling with mental and/or substance use disorders, you can call the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration's free and confidential treatment referral and information service at 1-800-662-HELP (4357). It's available 24/7 in English and Spanish (TTY: 1-800-487-4889) .

Contributing: Sameen Chaudhry, USA TODAY

articles.summary: Jessica Chastain's Apple TV series "The Savant" reportedly has a Spring 2027 release date after being postponed following Charlie Kirk's assassination.
articles.body: Apple TV's "The Savant" has a release date after it was postponed in September 2025, shortly after Turning Point USA co-founder Charlie Kirk was killed while speaking at a college campus event that same month. The show will be released in the spring of 2027, as reported by Deadline and Variety. A source confirmed the release timing to Fox News Digital. "The Savant" was set to premiere in September 2025 and followed an undercover investigator, played by Jessica Chastain, as she "infiltrates online hate groups in an effort to stop domestic extremists before they act," according to the show’s synopsis. "We appreciate your understanding and look forward to releasing the series at a future date." At the time, Apple TV did not provide details of its decision. However, the show would have premiered two weeks after Kirk was shot and killed in what authorities described as an ideologically motivated attack. Kirk’s alleged assassin was reported to have had a "leftist ideology" and harbored hatred against Kirk specifically. Sensori.Ai founder Dr. A.K. Pradeep said successful politicians tend to trigger a fight-or-flight response within the limbic system of the voter. "Corporations, unlike politicians, generally shy away from anything that triggers limbic responses. Anything that can trigger a limbic system response is the last thing Apple would want to be associated with," he said. "Apple wants to be associated with Consumer Desire, and not Consumer Limbic responses. This is the real reason for the decision." HOW THE MEDIA, IN THE DIGITAL AGE, HELP FUEL A CLIMATE OF ANGER AND VIOLENCE Chastain, an executive producer of "The Savant" as well as a star in it, spoke out against the decision to postpone in a Sept. 24, 2025, post to social media. She said she did not align with the decision. "In the last five years since we’ve been making the show, we’ve seen an unfortunate amount of violence in the United States: the kidnapping attempt on Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer; the January 6th attack on the Capitol; the assassination attempts on President Trump; the political assassinations of Democratic representatives in Minnesota; the attack on Speaker Pelosi’s husband; the assassination of conservative commentator Charlie Kirk; the recent shooting at an ABC affiliate station in California; and over 300 school shootings across this country," she wrote on Instagram at the time. "These incidents, though far from encompassing the full range of violence witnessed in the United States, illustrate a broader mindset that crosses the political spectrum and must be confronted. I’ve never shied away from difficult subjects, and while I wish this show wasn’t so relevant, unfortunately it is." Her post continued, "‘The Savant’ is about the heroes who work every day to stop violence before it happens, and honoring their courage feels more urgent than ever."
